# QNET — Queen's Nuclear Engineering Team

> Canada's only nuclear student design team, turning reactor theory into hands-on builds.

QNET (Queen's Nuclear Engineering Team) is a student design team at Queen's University in Kingston, Ontario, Canada, founded in 2026.

## Pages

- [Home](https://queensnuclear.ca/): Mission, news, and what the team does
- [About](https://queensnuclear.ca/about): Mission, 4-phase roadmap (Foundation → Build-Up → Launch → Future, through 2027+), and core values (Nuclear First; Interdisciplinary by Design; Built to Scale)
- [Teams](https://queensnuclear.ca/teams): Executive and sub-team members (Mechanical, Electrical, Software, Research, Materials, Operations)
- [QNET School](https://queensnuclear.ca/school): Nuclear education program with two pillars — General School (for all members) and Sub-Team Training (project-specific skills); lessons so far cover radiation basics, protection and detection, nuclear reactions and reactor basics, and reactor physics; first reactor tour completed October 23, 2026 at the SLOWPOKE-2 reactor at the Royal Military College of Canada (with photos); capstone design contest with up to $500 prize, with this year's capstone project being created by AtkinsRéalis; sponsors are scheduling guest lectures; Coursera & IAEA certification resources
- [CANDU® Cooling System](https://queensnuclear.ca/candu-cooling-system): 2026–2027 flagship build, selected by general member vote on September 24, 2026 (38 votes, ahead of gamma-ray imaging with 23 and a nuclear cleanup rover with 12) — the CANDU® Cooling System, a bench-scale natural-circulation reactor cooling loop with a backup pump, a bought heat exchanger feeding a secondary glycol loop, clear polymer piping, atmospheric pressure, and Raspberry Pi control with a hardwired E-stop (schedule: design in fall 2026, design freeze November 29, parts ordered in December, building in January, assembly and leak testing in February, testing and reports in March); roles for all five sub-teams — plus the Materials sub-team's independent study tracks
- [Join](https://queensnuclear.ca/join): Recruitment — open to every Queen's student with no application or interview; members join one of five sub-teams
- [Sponsors](https://queensnuclear.ca/sponsors): Sponsorship tiers — Kinetic ($50–$199), Thermal ($200–$499), Fission ($500–$1,499), Fusion ($1,500+, "Inaugural Partner"); contact qnet.sponsorship@engsoc.queensu.ca

## Key facts 

- Ratified by EngSoc Council in September 2026; 100+ members
- Upcoming: MECH 485 seminar, Friday, December 11, 2026, 8:30 AM, Mitchell Hall — QNET will have a booth
- Five sub-teams: Mechanical (CAD, 3D printing, structural design); Electrical (PCB design, power, sensing); Software (control logic, firmware, UI, IoT); Research (technical reports, reviews, case studies); Materials (material selection, degradation modeling, safety analysis)
- End-of-year demonstration in front of sponsors and nuclear industry professionals
- Socials: [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/queensnuclear/), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/queensnuclear/), [GitHub](https://github.com/qnuclear)
